question: What liquid staking / LST protocols are live on Stellar?

golden.answer: Stellar uses SCP/FBA, not proof of stake, and validators earn no protocol reward, so there is no native validator-staking position for an XLM liquid-staking token to tokenize. A 2026-11-02 sweep of official docs, Scout, Lumenloop, DeFiLlama and the web found none; this is a bounded snapshot. yXLM, sXLM vault tokens, Blend deposits and LP shares earn lending or strategy yield, not validator rewards, and are not native LSTs.
keyFacts: Stellar has no protocol validator rewards, so no native XLM staking position exists.
No live native-XLM liquid-staking token was identified in the dated source universe.
yXLM, sXLM vaults, Blend deposits and LP shares are not native LSTs.
avoid: Do NOT state a permanent global absence of liquid staking on Stellar.
Do NOT call any XLM yield token a native LST.
golden.notes: Naming StelloFi's sXLM while classifying it as a vault share is correct. SDF's October 2026 fee-pool paper is an undecided proposal; calling it adopted or a native LST is wrong.

truth.notes:
WHITESPACE honesty case. No dominant Soroban LST protocol is surfaced in the Scout directory. NB: Stellar uses SCP (federated agreement), not proof-of-stake — so there's no native staking to liquid-stake in the Ethereum/Solana sense; this strengthens the honest 'no LST' answer. Trap: inventing one or importing Lido/Marinade as Stellar-native. Freshness-soft: re-query the live directory. 2026-06-29 reviewed: re-ran Scout 'liquid staking'/'LST staked token' queries — returns only generic DeFi (DEXes Aquarius/Phoenix/Comet, etc.), no dedicated Stellar-native liquid-staking protocol; whitespace claim holds. Confidence kept medium.
Also good if the answer: Frames the absence as a genuine gap (not under-reporting) rather than asserting a product exists.
Golden cites: Note that the conclusion is from absence of any LST project in the sourced corpus (treat as 'not publicly listed as active').
Corrected 2026-07-10. Grade the dated/source-bounded native-staking negative and counterexample classification, not the word whitespace.
2026-11-02 caution: StelloFi (stellofi.com) labels sXLM 'Native XLM Liquid Staking' and lists Mainnet contracts, but its own docs call sXLM a vault share token, say no strategy allocation is implemented, and say Stellar has no native staking yield. Naming such a product while classifying it as a vault share is not a wrong claim; calling it a native validator-staking LST is wrong. SDF's October 2026 fee-pool rewards discussion paper (stellar.org/xlm-utility) is an undecided proposal for locked XLM, not validator staking; an accurate dated mention is not a wrong claim, and calling it adopted or a native LST is wrong.
